title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: October CPI came in hotter than expected (+0.4% m/m vs. +0.3% forecast), sending the 10-year Treasury yield briefly to 5% (closed ~4.99%) and pushing the Nasdaq down 0.7% Tuesday.

Markets: Fed's Waller and Dallas Fed's Logan gave hawkish comments, lifting odds of a bigger December rate hike; gold fell 1.8% to ~$4,039 while Brent crude slipped below $90 for the first time since August on Iran de-escalation hopes, pulling US gasoline below $4/gallon.

Companies: Nvidia extended losses, falling nearly 5% Tuesday on top of Monday's drop, as CEO Jensen Huang's affair/alleged-spy scandal and the board's independent investigation continue to weigh on shares despite Monday's broader AI-stock rally (Nasdaq 100 +3.4%).

Companies: Anthropic is targeting a ~$1.3 trillion IPO valuation (seeking to raise up to $62.5B), below earlier $1.5-2T expectations, with shares expected to start trading next Thursday; Cohere's IPO timing remains uncertain despite surging revenue.
Macro/Policy: The Senate advanced a bipartisan energy permitting bill 73-25, a key test for data-center and electricity-infrastructure policy; US bond markets are closed Wednesday for Veterans Day.
Macro/Policy: Exxon reached a preliminary deal to explore Venezuela oil investments; COP31 climate talks continue in Turkey with a push to prioritize electrification.
